messages:
leah: SafeSend hit a sustained wave of 429s during their nightly sync at ~00:00 UTC. Customer says it lasts ~90s every night. attaching excerpts from their logs.
safe_send_ops: yep — our job kicks off 00:00 UTC, 600 workers, each streams ~6 requests/sec for ~20s. We see a bunch of 429s with Retry-After: 60. header dumps below.
safe_send_ops: ```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\nRetry-After: 60\nX-RateLimit-Limit: 1200/min\nX-RateLimit-Remaining: 0\nX-RateLimit-Reset: 1712467959```\nwe hit RequestsPerMinute ~42000 for that minute
maria: thanks. two quick checks: which tenant id / API key? are they on free/standard? also, do they stream long-lived connections or short requests? that matters for inflight-slot math.
safe_send_ops: tenant id: ss-prod-01, standard plan. short requests (100-200ms) but many parallel TCP connections from our job farm.
jason: sounds like classic top-of-minute folding + high concurrency. minute bucket sees a huge spike when all cron workers align. the platform enforces tenant-level RPM (requests/min) and TPM (tokens/min). header shows limit 1200/min — that’s per-route or per-tenant? leah: for this customer it's tenant-wide default, route-level also applies but they are hitting the tenant RPM first.
maria: repro idea: run a short parallel load to recreate folding: ```for i in $(seq 1 600); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" https://api.redwood-inference.test/v1/generate & done; wait``` this will fold into a single minute and likely trigger 429s.
leah: also try a slightly spread run to confirm smoothing helps: ```seq 1 600 | xargs -n1 -P50 -I{} bash -c 'sleep $(python -c "import random; print(random.random()*59)"); curl -s -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" https://api.redwood-inference.test/v1/generate'``` if that reduces 429 rate then it's a client-side alignment issue.
safe_send_ops: we can test that. quick question — why is Retry-After 60? our flurry is ~20s, shouldn't the penalty be shorter?
maria: Retry-After is often set to 60 for tenant-level throttles to let the minute window rotate. it’s not punitive, just conservative. also X-RateLimit-Reset tells when the bucket resets. in your header X-RateLimit-Reset ~ 1712467959 indicates next window.
jason: ops note: client-side fixes first: stagger cron start times, add jitter, cap parallelism per worker, exponential backoff with full jitter. short-term we can apply a temporary tenant RPM bump for them while they refactor.
leah: action items:
- safe_send_ops: run the spread test and paste results (assigned: safe_send_ops)
- maria: prepare a temporary quota increase for ss-prod-01 and timeframe (assigned: maria)
- jason: draft guidance snippet for cron jitter + code sample for their runbook (assigned: jason)
- deploy-bot: if we bump quota, ensure monitor alert for CPU/GPU and token spend
deploy-bot: noted — requested quota change ticket #Q-8892, pending approval.
safe_send_ops: test results: spread test reduced 429 rate from ~70% of requests to ~5%. looks promising. we can roll jitter into tomorrow's deploy.
maria: great — I'll provision a +2x RPM for a 24h window while you ship the jitter change. if we still see bursts after jitter, we should consider Dedicated capacity for sustained high parallelism.
jason: small code snippet for jitter (python): ```import time, random\ndef send():\n  time.sleep(random.random()*30)\n  # call API``` add per-worker semaphore to limit concurrency to ~20 per host.
leah: also recommended: include X-Client-Bucket header if they want us to route requests to separate minutely buckets (experimental). reach out to me if they'd like us to enable it.
safe_send_ops: thanks all. rolling jitter + rpm bump plan sounds good. i'll post follow-up tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
maria: leaving a short postmortem w/ steps for other tenants in case they copy this pattern. tl;dr: "top-of-minute cron fanout -> RPM fold -> 429s. Fix: stagger + client backoff or upgrade capacity." :memo:
leah: closing for now, will reopen if 429s persist after the changes. :eyes:
